title: dedicated-fleet-capacity-deficit-debrief-and-corrective-backlog
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary: On 2025-11-17 at ~03:12 UTC a staged rollout of the autoscaler controller (change set: autoscaler-v2.7.3) caused unexpected tokenization of capacity signals, leading to sustained dedicated pool throughput degradation. Affected customers saw median throughput fall ~18-25% for impacted pools and latency p95 climb from ~120ms to ~520ms. This ticket captures the debrief, immediate mitigations applied, root cause analysis, and a prioritized corrective backlog to prevent recurrence.

Scope: 4 dedicated GPU pools in us-west-2 (legacy-pool-*), ~12% of committed reserved units during the incident window. No data exfiltration; primary impact is availability and SLA breaches for a small set of enterprise customers on dedicated plans.
timeline: 2025-11-17 03:12 UTC - autoscaler-v2.7.3 rollout started via canary ship to us-west-2
2025-11-17 03:27 UTC - alert: dedicated-pool-queue-length > 2x baseline (SLO guard triggered)
2025-11-17 03:33 UTC - engineering on-call paged; initial mitigation: rollback autoscaler canary
2025-11-17 03:45 UTC - rollback completed; backend reported partial recoveries but some pools remained degraded
2025-11-17 04:10 UTC - emergency temporary augmentation: injected headroom by spinning warm standby nodes for affected pools
2025-11-17 05:02 UTC - p95 latency returned ~180-240ms; formal incident command closed at 06:00 UTC with monitoring in watch
root_cause_summary: Change to the autoscaler controller altered the smoothing window for ingress signals and introduced a regression in aggregate capacity scoring when the inbound request mix had high variance in sequence length. The new scoring amplified short-term drops and prevented the controller from scaling up quickly when backlog increased. Additional contributing factors: insufficient telemetry on per-sequence-length request proportions and an overly aggressive batching policy that reduced effective concurrency during bursts.
mitigation_steps: 1) Immediate rollback of autoscaler-v2.7.3 canary and reinstatement of previous stable controller (v2.7.2). 2) Emergency warm-standby node allocation for affected pools and temporary elevation of burst capacity quota for affected customers. 3) Short term throttle policy adjustment to lower batching aggressiveness for high-variance workloads. 4) Post-rollback monitoring window extended to 72 hours with custom dashboards for sequence-length distribution.
action_items: A1 - Add per-sequence-length telemetry to capacity metrics (owner: Priya Menon) - due 2025-11-30
A2 - Implement a regression test for autoscaler controller that simulates high variance request mixes (owner: Marco Diaz) - due 2025-12-06
A3 - Harden rollout process to require canary hold time + synthetic workload injection before promotion (owner: Release Eng - Samir Patel) - due 2025-12-04
A4 - Create SLO-aware emergency augmentation runbook for Dedicated with exact steps and RBAC roles (owner: Ops - Elena Rossi) - due 2025-11-28
A5 - Revisit batching defaults with runtime team and provide workload classes to prevent underutilization during bursts (owner: Runtime - Yuna Park) - due 2025-12-10
A6 - Customer comms: notify impacted enterprise customers with RCA and timeline (owner: CS - Miguel Santos) - due 2025-11-26
acceptance_criteria: Per-sequence-length telemetry available in console and linked to dedicated pool dashboards
Autoscaler regression test added to CI and runs on PRs for controller changes
New rollout gating policy merged into release automation and verified in a dry-run
Emergency augmentation runbook published in ops playbook and validated by one drill
comments: 2025-11-17 06:20 - Marco Diaz: Initial rollback succeeded but residual queueing observed. Allocated warm standbys; looking at signal smoothing parameters.
2025-11-18 10:12 - Priya Menon: Telemetry scaffold pushed - collecting sequence-length histograms at 1m resolution. Dashboards link: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/seq-hist-51720
2025-11-19 14:45 - Samir Patel: Release gating RFC drafted - requires synthetic injection + 15m canary hold. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/3281
2025-11-24 16:05 - Yuna Park: Batching knob added behind feature flag; will test with replay harness next week
2025-11-25 08:11 - Miguel Santos: Customer comms template approved; outreach scheduled for 2025-11-26
retro_notes: Lessons learned: (1) Telemetry gaps obscured the true driver (sequence-length mix) — prioritize richer workload signals; (2) Rollouts must include synthetic traffic that matches customer diversity; (3) Batching heuristics need workload-class awareness. Decisions: require sequence-length histograms in all dedicated pool telemetry before any autoscaler change is promoted; add a mandatory canary-synthetic verification step. Long-term: evaluate a two-tier autoscaler that separates short-lived burst handling from steady-state scaling to reduce sensitivity to transient variance.
next_steps: Track A1-A6 as separate subtasks, validate mitigations in staging by 2025-12-04, schedule an ops drill to practice emergency augmentation on 2025-12-02, and deliver customer RCA on 2025-11-26.
